transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Rivera (VP Eng, Sentinel Health), Samir Patel (Cloud Architect), Monica Li (Security Lead), Jordan Hayes (DevOps)

[00:00] Alex: hey everybody, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with priya our se. quick check - does the time still work?
[00:05] Elena: yes thanks alex, this is elena. sorry running a little late, appreciate you doing this.
[00:10] Alex: no worries. goal for the call is to understand your networking constraints for a Private deployment - vpc peering, private endpoints, region requirements and any compliance must-haves. priya will cover the technical bits and i'll capture next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Priya: yep hi all. real quick, can you share high level of current infra - are you on AWS across the board? kubernetes? any transit gateway?
[00:25] Samir: yea we're fully on AWS. EKS for our services, some lambda. we have a hub-and-spoke using transit gateway in us-east-1 and us-west-2. most latency sensitive workloads are in us-east-1.
[00:33] Jordan: our CIDRs are overlapping in a few dev accounts but prod is clean - prod VPC is 10.10.0.0/16.
[00:38] Monica: quick security note, we need all traffic to be VPC-internal only, no public internet egress for inference payloads. also company compliance requires KMS integration and detailed audit logs for all model calls.
[00:49] Priya: got it. two possible patterns from redwood side - Private deployment with a private control plane in your VPC (we can deploy private endpoints and service ENIs) OR a peered deployment where our managed control plane peers into your VPC and traffic flows over peering / transit. main differences: Private (VPC-hosted) gives you full network ownership; peering is simpler to stand up initially but has egress/bandwidth considerations and requires CIDR compatibility.
[01:05] Elena: can you expand on egress? we don't want anything traversing internet gateways for PHI workloads.
[01:09] Priya: absolutely. with Private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) we can keep traffic within AWS network and expose a private NLB/ENI that lives in your subnet. For peering, traffic stays on the AWS backbone but you need to ensure routes and NAT behavior - if our service needs to pull model updates from an external repo, you'd have to allow that through an egress proxy or use VPC endpoints. we can also support VPC peering + route table restrictions to avoid internet egress.
[01:28] Samir: ok - how does that interact with KMS? we use AWS KMS with a key policy that restricts to our account. can redwood use a customer managed key or do we need to share keys?
[01:36] Alex: short answer: we support customer-managed KMS keys for encryption at rest and can integrate with your KMS via cross-account grants. additional options include hardware security module (HSM) integrations for higher compliance tiers. we'll send the exact architecture and key grant snippets.
[01:46] Monica: yes please. also SOC2 and ISO stuff - we need to see reports before pilot.
[01:50] Alex: absolutely, i'll attach SOC2 and relevant security docs.
[01:52] Priya: one other note on region constraints - if most clients are us-east-1, we can deploy the Private control plane there. question for you: do you need regional failover in another region for DR?
[02:00] Elena: we do - primary in us-east-1, secondary in us-west-2. we want less than 50ms p99 intra-region latency for inference served to east-coast customers.
[02:09] Priya: okay, we usually recommend colocating model-serving nodes in the same region as clients. for cross-region failover we can host standby replicas and use DNS failover or route53 weighted policies. note that model weights syncing across regions may incur transfer time; we can work with you on pre-warming and async replication.
[02:25] Jordan: what's the network footprint - do we need public IPs for the serving nodes?
[02:28] Priya: no public IPs required in Private deployment. we put private ENIs in your subnets. If you want outbound-only updates, you can use NAT Gateway or VPC endpoints for S3/ECR. For fully locked down env you can mirror model artifacts into your S3 and point the runtime at your internal store.
[02:44] Samir: model sizes are big - 30-70GB. how does bootstrap and KV cache warmup work without huge egress bills?
[02:50] Priya: good question. we support preloading model artifacts from your internal S3 to node-local storage, and we have delta sync to avoid full pulls on every restart. also quantized variants reduce footprint. caching (kv cache) is local and doesn't leave your VPC. there was a typo in one of our docs a while back where they wrote "K V cash" so apologies for that.
[03:06] Elena: what about IP allowlist - we need a stable set of IPs for firewall rules if peering is used.
[03:11] Alex: with PrivateLink we avoid IP churn because the ENIs are in your account. with peering we can provide a set of ASN and expected IP ranges, but peering will require you to accept route table entries. we typically provide a recommended CIDR and a short list of endpoints - will include in the doc.
[03:25] Monica: audit logs - we need per-call logging including request id, model version, timestamp, and user id. retention 13 months.
[03:33] Priya: we can emit audit logs to your CloudWatch/CloudTrail or to an S3 bucket. logs can be structured and include request-level metadata; retention is configurable on your side. we'll share the schema.
[03:44] Samir: latency numbers - what p50/p95 tokens per second can you guarantee for e.g. a 2B model on 1 GPU versus 8 GPU cluster?
[03:52] Priya: depends a lot on sequence length and batch. ballpark: single GPU for a small 2B can do low-latency calls ~50-80ms p50 for 128 tokens; larger clusters for throughput. we'll run a benchmark in your environment as part of the pilot and share concrete numbers.
[04:06] Elena: and cost sensitivity - we need cost per million tokens estimates and dedicated reserved pricing.
[04:10] Alex: yes we'll provide a pricing comparison Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted. typically Private has a higher upfront for infra but lower per-token when you control infra.
[04:18] Jordan: a practical question - who manages OS/security patches on the nodes if deployed in our VPC?
[04:23] Priya: in Private deployment we can offer two modes: managed nodes where Redwood handles runtime updates but your infra team approves AMIs and we do patch windows; or customer-managed nodes where you run our runtime container and handle OS patches. we'll outline both.
[04:36] Monica: SSO integration? we use Okta and need SAML and SCIM provisioning plus RBAC enforcement.
[04:41] Alex: supported. SCIM + SAML SSO is standard and we can map groups to roles in the Console/Private control plane.
[04:47] Samir: any hard requirements on VPC sizing, subnets?
[04:51] Priya: we recommend dedicated subnets per AZ for serving, at least /24 per subnet for autoscaling, and high MTU for model transfers. we'll include recommended sizes in the network diagram.
[04:59] Elena: timeline - we'd like a pilot in 3 weeks and production in 8-10 weeks after that if benchmarks look good.
[05:06] Alex: that's feasible. next steps I'll send the SOC2, KMS integration guide, and the peering/privatelink checklist. Priya will draft the network diagram and a proposed pilot runbook. Samir to share CIDRs.
[05:18] Jordan: can we get a hands-on walkthrough of the control plane before pilot?
[05:21] Priya: yes we can schedule a 60-minute demo of the Private console and rollout controls - i'll reach out with times.
[05:27] Elena: perfect. appreciate the clarity - couple of small clarifications on model sync and audit schema and then we'll sign off with security once docs are in.
[05:36] Alex: great. we'll follow up via email with attachments. thanks everyone.

Meeting end.
